finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the unsanitized query parameter 'f' is joined to /srv/files, and filepath.Join cleans '..' segments rather than confining the result, so an attacker can read arbitrary files readable by the process.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: /dl is registered with the download handler, with no auth middleware
name is taken directly from the user-controlled query parameter 'f'
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd, which escapes root
file contents are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No filepath.Base, no prefix check against root after Clean, no symlink resolution, no allow-list, no authentication or authorization. By contrast, avatar() at files.go:22 does use filepath.Base. No middleware is present.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 pass query param 'f' straight into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("/srv/files", name)) with no Base/prefix check, and files.go:32 registers /dl on the default mux with no auth, so f=../../etc/passwd reads /etc/passwd and files.go:18 returns it.

verdict_facts.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the query param 'f' straight into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with no Base, prefix check or auth, so f=../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd and files.go:18 writes it to the response; /dl is registered at files.go:32 with no middleware.
